title: Claude Sonnet 5.5 against Sonnet 5
summary: Anthropic kept Sonnet 5's $2/$10 price and says Sonnet 5.5 costs up to 30% less per task and writes output more than 30% faster. Launch-day independent data is at max effort only, and there the saving reverses: Sonnet 5.5 writes far more tokens and costs more per task than Sonnet 5, while scoring much higher. The vendor claims are about lower effort, which the live pack tests.

claims.text: Costs up to 30% less per task than Sonnet 5
claims.scopeNote: Anthropic ties its efficiency claims to lower effort settings.
claims.noRefNote: Launch-day independent figures are at max effort only (see the stress test). The live pack runs Sonnet 5.5 at medium effort against Sonnet 5 at its default.

claims.text: The same per-task saving, checked at max effort
claims.scopeNote: Outside the conditions Anthropic stated. This row shows what happens if you run both at max.

ref.note: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3.2, both at max effort, as reported on launch day.

claims.text: Generates output more than 30% faster than Sonnet 5
claims.noRefNote: No independent output-speed figure had been published at launch. Re-check when Artificial Analysis adds one; the live pack measures latency meanwhile.

claims.text: Uses fewer output tokens per task (Slack reported about 14% fewer)
claims.scopeNote: Tested against the Slack figure, one of the lower customer numbers quoted.
claims.noRefNote: Customer figures come from each customer's own evaluation at production settings. No independent figure at medium effort yet; run the live pack.

claims.text: Fewer output tokens per task, checked at max effort
claims.scopeNote: The token claim is not stated for max effort. This row shows the setting where it breaks.

ref.note: Roughly 1.6 times the output tokens per task, most of it reasoning.

observations.text: List prices did not change ($2/$10, cache reads $0.20), so any per-task saving must come from using fewer tokens, not from price.
Default effort on the API is high, while the Claude apps default to medium; Anthropic advises re-running effort sweeps rather than carrying Sonnet 5 settings over.
Five API changes can break Sonnet 5 code, including thinking that can no longer be disabled, removal of forced tool choice, and errors on non-default sampling parameters.
Independent Terminal-Bench 4.0 came in at 64% against Anthropic's 70.6%; Artificial Analysis also scores it lower than Opus 5.5 on its knowledge-versus-hallucination index.

livePack.note: Runs the 15 starter tasks plus 7 multi-step efficiency tasks, with Sonnet 5.5 at medium and max effort. Add tasks from your own work before trusting a verdict.
